items.summary_html: Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's latest fast and low-cost model. The model is priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens up to 100,000 tokens, after which the price increases 5x. Under 100,000 tokens, Haiku is the same price as GPT-6 Luna and reports higher benchmark scores, but above 100,000 tokens, Luna looks like a much better deal.
items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI recently released 372 breakthrough results in the field of mathematics. However, it appears no human has understood any of the proofs yet. Experts reading the proofs say the papers are so horribly written they're impossible to read without AI help. The citations are also often irrelevant and confusing.
items.title: The Mathocalypse (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Biohub, a nonprofit co-founded by Mark Zuckerberg, is working with the Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health, and other funding partners to invest $1.8 billion in building biological data ready for AI models. The investment is aimed at providing data sets that allow researchers to use AI models to find new ways of preventing and treating diseases. The DOE will invest more than $500 million across five years in lab measurement, modeling, and computation to build an AI-ready open data resource; the NIH will coordinate the contribution of relevant datasets, repositories, and knowledge bases; and Biohub will work with the NIH to standardize the datasets for AI model training.
items.title: Zuckerberg's Biohub Partners With DOE, NIH to Invest $1.8 Billion in Biological Data for AI Models (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Two independent teams in Vienna and Beijing have simultaneously built the first clocks that keep time by counting the squishing and unsquishing of the atomic nuclei of thorium. The clocks are so precise that they only lose one second once every few million years or so. Nuclear clocks have the ability to search for certain kinds of dark matter. If a particle of dark matter passes through the thorium nuclei, it could register as a wobble in the nuclear clock's otherwise steady tick-tock.
items.title: In Vienna and Beijing, the First Nuclear Clocks Begin to Tick (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Super ICs gain influence by repeatedly doing the unglamorous things. Over time, making the work better, making the story clearer, and making it easier for other people to succeed changes how people behave around you. Authority is a natural side effect of being the person others rely on. Focus on sharpening your craft, turning ideas into stories people can retell, packaging your thinking so it travels without you, and helping your peers hit their goals.
items.title: Influence without authority (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Readers need a compelling reason quickly to continue reading. The reader should be able to read an article from start to finish without clicking links or hovering for tooltips. Avoid presenting articles as a follow-up to a previous article. Drop the formality and write the way you speak in real life. Test articles in mobile view, and use browser testing tools to find low-contrast text to improve visibility.
items.title: Anti-Patterns in Software Blogging (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Super Smash Bros. Melee's decompilation reached 100% on September 7. Within hours, this developer was wearing a Meta Quest and watching Fox and Marth fight in their apartment. The screen recording of the fight passed a hundred thousand views in just a few days. This article details how the developer brought the match into the headset.
items.title: I Put Smash Bros Melee in My Living Room (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Artcraft released a suite of open-source apps over the weekend aimed at recreating the user interface and tools found in Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. The developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to create the software. The apps are still in a 'super early alpha' state, but the developer believes that they will be able to produce something as functional as anything Adobe has ever put out. They claim they will be able to reach 99% feature parity within months.
items.title: “Software is over”: Bold AI developer takes aim at Adobe with open source clones (3 minute read)

SpaceX says the new spectrum will help cover places satellite links can't reach. SpaceX still needs some terrestrial infrastructure to use the spectrum for mobile coverage.
items.title: SpaceX Makes Big Play to Become a Wireless Carrier (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Atomic Machines is building AI technology that can discover new ways of designing extremely small devices. It is building an automated manufacturing system that turns computer code into a physical device. The company aims to revamp the field of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), tiny devices made of both electrical and mechanical components. These devices are traditionally manufactured like computer chips, but this limits the possibilities of the technology to the physical properties of a semiconductor.
items.title: The Start-Up That Wants to Build ‘Microrobots' With AI (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Amazon's Leo project is nearing several critical milestones. The company recently manufactured its 1,000th satellite and has reached the point where it can build a handful of satellites every day. The Vulcan's upcoming return-to-flight mission will carry Amazon Leo satellites, and another Vulcan rocket is currently being prepared to launch this year with more Amazon satellites. The company is just weeks away from offering a commercial space broadband service for the first time.
items.title: Amazon builds 1,000th satellite, will launch space internet service by end of year (19 minute read)

They can be used to add custom features to Claude Code. Mods run inside Claude Code, so they can do things that hooks, skills, status lines, and MCP servers can't, like redraw Claude Code's own interface, step into a tool call or request, and share data between hooks.

Alpha 1 is on npm and jsDelivr right now. Bootstrap 6 requires Chrome and Edge 130, Firefox 132, and Safari 18. Bootstrap 5 remains available and supported.

The centerpiece will be a smart home hub called the HomeView that essentially serves as the Siri command center for an Apple-powered household. There will be a countertop model with a metal base and a wall-mounted version with a flat, square base that sits against the wall beneath the display. The HomeView will only support a limited selection of Apple applications, and there will be no App Store for downloading additional software.
items.title: Apple Is About to Close the Biggest Hole In Its Ecosystem With HomeView (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Shenzhen opened access for nighttime deliveries by driverless vehicles in March. Night operations make otherwise idle vehicles and infrastructure productive. It also means quieter roads, reduced pedestrian traffic, and lower congestion. Driverless vehicles eliminate the cost of a human: they don't need night shift wages, they don't get tired, and they don't need to be paid extra for driving in the rain.
items.title: China's Delivery Robots Are Learning to Tackle the Night Shift (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Borrowing an idea from one research discipline to solve a problem in another is an age-old scientific trick. However, such clever leaps are rare because researchers don't tend to spend their time researching fields outside of their expertise. AI can easily hop between fields. BootLoops is a harness that can spot and solve problems in seemingly unrelated fields that share the same mathematical structures at massive scale. Researchers recently released 36 preprints produced with BootLoops covering a wide range of topics, including figuring out the age of sunspots, analyzing government health policies, and attempting to decipher a mysterious medieval manuscript.
items.title: Problems in 22 scientific fields had solutions hiding in plain sight. An AI has found them (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Not learning to use AI at this point is detrimental to your career. The tastes and desires in the employment market have changed. Teams that aren't working with AI will be replaced with workers who use AI. The job market might look tough, but it's much easier for workers who have been investing in themselves.
items.title: If your team is too busy doing their 'normal job' to experiment with AI, you're preparing them to be replaced (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: GitHub is rebuilding its Git storage architecture from scratch. Early internal testing shows a promising 35x write improvement. The plan involves decoupling writes from reads, offloading maintenance, and letting object storage manage redundancy. The change won't alter developer workflows, review processes, or security controls.
items.title: So long, Spokes: GitHub rewrites storage to restore reliability, just in time for agentic hordes (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic entered into a deal worth up to $45 billion earlier this year to lease computing power from SpaceX. The unlikely alliance illustrates the industry's increasingly desperate scramble for compute. Demand is outstripping supply, and prices are rising, causing tech companies to strike deals with rivals. Venture-capital firms are helping startups obtain computing capacity.

The new models combine Active Memory, which carries important personal context across conversations and retrieves relevant details when a task calls for them, with Active Focus, a feature designed to keep the model working through difficult goals by trying alternative approaches, handling blockers, adapting to new information, requesting clarification when needed, and checking before important actions. Meta says Muse Wonder is its most aligned model yet.
items.title: Meta launches Muse Wonder and Wonder Full for AI agents (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft's newest iteration of its Maia chips will start rolling out next year. The Maia 300 is designed to handle inference. Microsoft expects to stock multiple gigawatts of the chips at its server farms. The Maia 300 delivers 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. Microsoft isn't currently planning to rent the underlying computing power of Maia chips directly to its cloud customers.
items.title: Microsoft Prepares to Put Gigawatts of Its Chips in Data Centers (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Amazon already has more than a million robots working in its warehouses, and it is poised to significantly grow that robotic fleet in the coming years. Amazon is also the second largest corporate employer in the world. The company's executives say the growing robot fleet has eased the burden on its human workforce, but labor advocacy groups and independent researchers say the warehouse automation is not all upside for the humans working alongside robots. It can get complicated when humans are expected to keep pace with their robotic counterparts.
items.title: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What's next for human employees? (23 minute read)

items.summary_html: Research suggests that human thought is not purely linguistic. More brain regions light up than just the areas associated with language when we are thinking. Language may be how we communicate about the world, but our thoughts seem to draw on many other areas outside of the brain's language networks. AI's ability to translate effectively means that it can understand, in some sense.
items.title: Is ‘Attention' the Essence of Intelligence? (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Co-browsing needs to work really well for users for the web to succeed in the agentic age. It is the only model where the developer and the user maintain control over the experience, and where the web remains the web. WebMCP enables sites to provide agents with direct JavaScript tools they can call to accomplish tasks, which makes direct interaction significantly faster, better, and cheaper. It circumvents the slowness and awkwardness of AI agents trying to figure out how to interact with sites.
items.title: Why WebMCP matters (12 minute read)

They also talk about the creation of Meta Superintelligence Labs, the decision to execute a complete talent reboot, and what it feels like to make an over $100 billion CapEx commitment before knowing if the model will work. The interview explores the architecture of Muse Wonder and lays out Meta's vision for agentic commerce, hardware form factors like smart glasses, and why superintelligence belongs in the hands of billions.
items.title: Muse Wonder: Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI (130 minute read)

Several creators have returned to the platform after boycotting it not because they prefer to use it, but because the realities of their businesses dictate that they should, if not must. items.summary_html: Cortex replaced a Lucene-based search architecture with PostgreSQL full-text search, a custom query parser, weighted ranking, and CDC-fed indexes. The change cut public API p95 latency from 13.3 seconds to 1.54 seconds, reduced total memory use by about 40%, and made most edits searchable within seconds.
items.title: A Hitchhiker's Guide to Postgres Text Search (14 minute read)

items.title: Anti-Patterns in Software Blogging (10 minute read)

Chrome's reach could make the format mainstream, especially for high-fidelity photography, lossless compression, progressive decoding, and lossless JPEG transcoding.
items.title: JPEG XL Finally Lands in Chrome! (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The essay examines five objections to AI coding: code as art, job displacement, dehumanizing work, rule-based views of software engineering, and support for powerful AI companies. It argues that several critiques depend on debatable assumptions about what software work is for, while locating the strongest human concern in labor relations and control of production.
items.title: Reasons to Dislike AI Coding (3 minute read)

items.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for Everyone (12 minute read)

Anthropic says average running costs are about 75% lower than Haiku 4.5, with adjustable effort and availability across its platform, AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure.

items.title: Docker Agent (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Agentic development changes the ideal linter because automated checks run on nearly every coding turn and agents can act on rules that humans might find too noisy. Ultracite pairs fast tools such as Oxlint and Oxfmt with strict rules and agent instructions, while keeping judgment-heavy questions for review.
items.title: The Agentic Development Loop (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: A remote Upstash Box gives Grok Bot a shell, persistent filesystem, GitHub integration, public previews, schedules, snapshots, and optional browser automation through MCP. The examples show it building a live app, cloning and fixing repositories, and turning a Slack report into a Linear ticket and pull request from a phone.
items.title: I Gave Grok Bot a Remote Computer (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Vanguard's password reset form silently truncated pasted passwords at 20 characters, while its login form accepted the full value and then rejected it as incorrect. The incident shows why password length limits should be validated visibly in JavaScript or on the server instead of using an HTML maxlength attribute that changes the submitted credential.
items.title: input type="password" maxlength="20" Prevents Me from Logging into Vanguard (2 minute read)

The hard-won lessons cover queued follow-ups, deterministic network controls, Docker-capable custom images, and designing every run to survive the loss of its sandbox.
items.title: We built our own cloud agents runtime. Here's what we learned (11 minute read)

It also explains how streaming recompiles partial output, preserves keyed state, and sends server-resolved data such as images separately from model text.

It surfaces slow Gemma 4 timings, position bias, context limits, probability semantics, and differences between Chrome's prototype and MediaPipe's DecisionMaker.
items.title: Chrome Decisions API: the prompts, limits, engines and code reviews behind DecisionModel (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: As AI makes code production cheap, the scarce work shifts to choosing priorities, reviewing product behavior, maintaining architecture, and owning outcomes in production. Senior engineers create leverage by turning repeated review feedback into guidance and deterministic lint rules while keeping human judgment for business context.
items.title: When code is cheap, judgement becomes the job (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: A practical test gate checks agent-written changes on a clean machine before review by reinstalling from scratch, running the full suite three times, rejecting removed or skipped tests, and restoring the base branch's tests against the new code. Running the same gate inside the agent loop turns failures into immediate repair instructions while an independent CI run keeps the verdict outside the agent's control.
items.title: Don't merge what you didn't run: a test gate for agent-written code (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Treg acts as an OpenRouter for agent tools, giving agents one base URL and token for a catalog of metered provider endpoints plus team-owned APIs, CLIs, and skills. It can inject credentials server-side, expose tools through MCP and agent skills, and let teams share capabilities without placing provider keys in callers.
items.title: Treg (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Plannotator provides a local browser-based review surface for plans, Markdown, HTML artifacts, diffs, and pull requests produced by coding agents. Hooks and commands route annotations back to agents, with support for multiple agent harnesses and local-first storage by default.
items.title: Plannotator (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: A React Server Components flaw let an attacker force quadratic work while React rebuilt FormData for a server action, allowing a roughly 900 KB request to trigger 100 million string checks and block a Node.js event loop. The issue affects vulnerable React 19.0 to 19.2 releases and is fixed in 19.0.6, 19.1.7, and 19.2.6.
items.title: A Single POST Freezes Any Next.js Server (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Expo built a CI evaluation harness that measures whether coding agents discover relevant skills, follow their guidance, and produce working apps. Adding an overview skill raised sessions loading at least one downstream Expo skill from 9% to 55%, while catalog crowding tests showed why names and opening descriptions must survive truncation.
items.title: Your skills need an evaluation mechanism (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: The origin story of Zotero shows how years of conversation, prototypes, and collaboration helped a team of historians discover what durable research software should become. Its path from Web Scrapbook and Scribe to a browser-aware tool used by millions argues that clear product vision can require slow communal formation, even when implementation itself becomes cheap.
items.title: The Slow Formation of Durable Software (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: calc-input lets forms accept arithmetic expressions, shows formulas on focus and results on blur, and uses a safe parser plus native form validation instead of eval().
items.title: calc-input, a custom input element that accepts mathematical formulas (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Google study found most internal open source package updates take four hours or less, while local patches, dependencies, and upstream contributor counts better predicted difficult updates than package age or internal adoption.
items.title: How much does it cost to use open source software? (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: A display-only flicker that browser captures could not reproduce was traced to full-width tile repaints, then reduced from 267 page-tile repaints to 9 by promoting only the changing timeline elements to their own composited layers.
items.title: The Bug Only My Screen Could See (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: video-shotcraft turns coding agents into a Remotion-based motion studio with 157 shot recipes, 214 motion previews, editable templates, sound design guidance, and a browser workbench.
items.title: video-shotcraft (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: A Qwen3-1.7B walkthrough turns multiple-choice questions into single-pass predictions by scoring only the allowed answer tokens. Fine-tuning improves accuracy on a 1,221-question CommonsenseQA sample from 59.4% to 62.4%, while temperature scaling makes the model's confidence better reflect its actual accuracy.
items.title: Build Your Own Decision Model (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Three production investigations, a latency regression, a memory leak, and a kernel-level hang, show how to steer coding agents through unfamiliar systems using runtime evidence. The framework separates facts from hypotheses, compares failures with a control, and requires every proposed cause to satisfy all known constraints. Adversarial reviews should seek contradictions, and reproductions must match the real failure's signals before they can be trusted.
items.title: How to Effectively Debug When You No Longer Understand the Code (63 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cockroach Labs structures coding agents around a teaching hospital, with reviewed plans, separate implementation and review roles, structured handoffs, and an audit before merge. The pipeline landed over a million lines of code in five months with seven reverts, and human approval became mandatory after the first autonomous week before the team used it to build customer-facing migration tooling.

Lower session costs encourage unattended chores, exploratory testing, and long planning sessions, with a more expensive model sometimes brought in for a final review.
items.title: Why Isn't the Industry Freaking Out About DeepSeek 4.1 Flash? (4 minute read)

items.title: Talorys (GitHub Repo)

Moving the scratch files to tmpfs cuts runtime from 73 minutes to 97 seconds, while workload-specific writeback tuning reaches about 100 seconds without moving them off disk.

In production, fewer than 2% of submissions are rejected as stale, with median submit latency below 1.7 seconds.

items.summary_html: AI code review will increasingly replace reading every diff, shifting human work toward requirements, acceptance testing, and ownership of releases. A trading-bot rounding bug illustrates the tradeoff: fast fixes do not erase losses or compensate for gaps in the specification.

items.summary_html: WebMCP lets websites expose JavaScript tools to agents, reducing the slow, brittle interaction of navigating through screenshots and DOM inspection while keeping users in a shared browser session. Permissions, human approval signals, and testing against complete agent systems remain open challenges.
items.title: Why WebMCP Matters (9 minute read)

Meta reports stronger performance on unfamiliar tasks from larger base models and plans a fuller safety report.

items.summary_html: Speculative Decoding is a technique where a small draft model proposes a likely draft sequence, and a big model verifies that sequence in parallel in a single forward pass. It enables the ability to look at many tokens at once and accept the ones that would have been generated by the big model. When the batch size is smaller than the optimal number of tokens, speculative decoding allows models to use 'free' compute to complete sequences faster. However, at high throughput, you could actually be wasting compute when you could be using that time to move memory.
items.title: Why is Speculative Decoding Fast? (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cheap-loop domains are domains where experiments are quick, deterministic, and cheap. Expensive-loop domains are restricted by real-world constraints or costs. Most high-value human labor is done in expensive-loop domains. Expensive-loop tasks require the ability to build theories, manage proxies, budget time and compute, and diagnose what went wrong when feedback is scarce, something models don't learn in cheap-loop training.
items.title: The Expensive-Loop Problem (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Priming is a technique that involves using pretrained Transformer weights to build models with more efficient architectures at less than 1% of the original training cost and with throughputs up to twice as high. It allows researchers to explore the design space, the layer type, the hybrid ratio, and layer placement cheaply and systematically. Every variant starts from the same strong initialization and requires minimal training compared to pretraining. Priming is not tied to a specific Transformer family or model class, and extending it to other models requires no algorithmic changes.
items.title: Can we change an AI model's architecture without retraining it from scratch? (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: On-policy distillation has become increasingly popular for transferring teacher capabilities to student models. Semi-OPD, which distills from offline rollouts generated by the initial student, can often outperform OPD in both accuracy and training efficiency. The choice between OPD and Semi-OPD depends on the alignment between the initial teacher and student. OPD is beneficial only when the two are highly aligned with high overlap ratios.
items.title: When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better (1 minute read)

items.title: Decision Models Cut Agent LLM Calls by 29.6% (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Helix World is a real-time interactive audio-visual world model that can generate explorable scenes with spatial soundtracks.
items.title: Meet Helix World: A Real-Time Audio-Visual World Model (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: AGENT-ENGINEER is an open-source plugin that enhances AI coding assistants, offering 11 skills, 4 subagents, and 5 hooks to tackle agent-engineering challenges.
items.title: Make Your Coding Assistant a 10x AI Engineer (13 minute read)

items.title: Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Highspeed Appears in ZCode Gray Release, With Users Reporting About 490 Tokens/s (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: TSMC reported revenue of $511.86 billion New Taiwan dollars for September, a 54.6% year-over-year increase. Demand for advanced AI chips, driven by customers like Nvidia and Apple, boosted sales. TSMC has also committed to using ASML's advanced lithography machines to enhance chip production.
items.title: TSMC's September sales surge year-over-year as AI drives chip demand (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Amazon built its 1,000th Leo broadband satellite at its Kirkland, Washington plant, which took six months to produce its first 27 and now turns out 27 a week. It builds propulsion in-house and borrowed consumer electronics methods to cut tests that took weeks down to hours. The bottleneck is launch: only 396 are in orbit against 3,232 needed, and the Vulcan grounding and a New Glenn pad explosion cost Amazon FCC spectrum priority.
items.title: Amazon builds its 1,000th Leo satellite at 27 a week, but only 396 are in orbit (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: IEEE Spectrum examines the up-to-$1B CHIPS R&D award finalized for IBM spinoff Anderon in September. IBM is matching that funding with $1B, while Anderon uses a 300mm Albany line and plans foundry services and process design kits for outside developers. The challenge is repeatable fabrication, including tighter control of Josephson junctions, rather than simply adding wafer capacity.
items.title: Anderon aims to industrialize quantum chip fabrication (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tensor virtualization decouples a tensor's logical layout from its physical GPU allocation, so one shader template replaces separate backend-specific codebases. For edge LLMs, ML Drift switches kernels between compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode, using a convolution-aligned KV cache layout and in-kernel activation quantization to skip memory roundtrips. It cut YouTube Shorts frame latency by up to 40%, and Google co-optimized it with Arm, Intel, and Qualcomm GPUs.
items.title: Google open-sources ML Drift, a GPU engine that runs one shader set across OpenCL, Metal, WebGPU, and OpenGL ES (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Scientists from the Harbin Institute of Technology developed a cement-based supercapacitor capable of powering small devices like LEDs. The device uses a 3D-printed electrode ink made from carbon nanotubes and cement, enabling fast energy discharge. Future research will enhance cold-weather performance, potentially allowing buildings to store energy and support smart environments.
items.title: Supercapacitor cement is key to buildings that store their own power (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Gartner predicts that over half of quantum startups will fail by 2030 due to a market unable to generate sufficient revenue. Despite this, companies are investing in quantum technologies for their potential business advantages, focusing on building expertise rather than waiting for technological maturity. The public sector and financial industries are expected to lead quantum computing investments, with spending reaching $245 million and $289 million by 2027 and 2028, respectively.
items.title: Too many quantum startups, too little money to keep them alive (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple gained a full percentage point in market share year-over-year as RAM price increases led to a 20% decrease in overall PC shipments. Despite this downturn, Apple was less affected than most competitors. With prices expected to worsen, Apple's resilience highlights its strong customer base willing to invest in new devices.
items.title: There's a hidden upside to the rampocalypse for Apple (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA expanded its Halos safety system from self-driving cars to robots with Halos for Robotics in June.
items.title: NVIDIA's Safety Stack for Physical AI (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: The toolchain covers synthetic data generation, training, simulation and validation, edge deployment, and continuous improvement.
items.title: AWS Launches an Open-Source Physical AI Toolchain for Robotics (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft's 15-inch Surface Laptop Ultra runs Nvidia's RTX Spark superchip, pairing up to a 20-core Grace CPU and Blackwell graphics with up to 128GB of unified memory, enough for local agents on models up to 120B parameters.
items.title: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra brings Nvidia's RTX Spark to a 15-inch, $2,600 laptop (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Who's building on-prem compute in 2026? It turns out a lot of people! Oxide Computer Company, which builds custom on-prem cloud compute systems, has closed a massive $445 million Series D funding round led by Eclipse, with participation from major investors including Jane Street, Atreides Management, and chipmaker AMD. The capital injection follows the startup achieving operational profitability and will be used to scale manufacturing capacity, secure raw material inventory, and fulfill a rapidly expanding order backlog for their commercial cloud computer racks.
items.title: Oxide Computer Company Secures $445M Series D Funding Round (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX agreed to buy up to 14 MHz of paired 800 MHz low-band spectrum, which penetrates buildings, and plans to deploy its own antennas on towers and rooftops to use it, with most existing phones already supporting the band. Separately, the FCC approved 15,000 more Starlink satellites optimized for 2 GHz. Together they point to a hybrid network, terrestrial indoors and satellite beyond towers. The deal needs FCC approval, and Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile shares fell roughly 6% on the news.
items.title: SpaceX buys 800 MHz low-band spectrum to pair terrestrial towers with 2 GHz Starlink satellites (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: In this rare peek under the hood, we get a glimpse of how Foxconn uses NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac, and Metropolis platforms to create physically accurate digital twins of manufacturing facilities that assemble next-generation AI server hardware. By simulating factory layouts, automated optical inspection systems, and autonomous mobile robot fleets in virtual environments before physical deployment, the company minimizes factory commissioning delays and boosts production efficiency. This approach showcases how system architects and automation specialists can leverage high-fidelity simulation to safely validate and optimize complex robotic workcells prior to hardware installation.
items.title: The Machines That Make the Machines: Advancing Industrial Digital Twins (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: After May's pad explosion destroyed its transporter-erector, Blue Origin is rebuilding LC-36 for vertical integration, loading New Glenn through the support tower alone, as with Starship. Crews destacked the tower, added cryogenic propellant plumbing on the ground, and have begun restacking modules, while the launch bridge is restored. Umbilicals and fairing access platforms haven't appeared yet. Bezos targets a December return to flight carrying Blue Ring, though he joked it could slip to December 31.
items.title: Blue Origin rebuilds LC-36 for vertical New Glenn integration, targeting a December return (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Nature Computational Science briefing describes an in situ learning method where photonic integrated circuits directly measure optical gradients, so diverse circuit layouts can be trained after they're built. That removes the need for a full digital model of the chip, which optical training normally leans on. The team demonstrated matrix design, multiwavelength computation, and rapid meta-learning on the hardware. Specifics like accuracy or energy figures aren't included.
items.title: Photonic chips learn after fabrication by measuring their own optical gradients (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: ScaRF-SLAM is a dense visual mapping system that pairs the reliability of classical visual SLAM with modern feed-forward geometric foundation models for 3D scene reconstruction from the Oxford Robot Dynamics Lab. By decoupling camera tracking from dense depth estimation and optimizing scale consistency across submaps, it achieves globally accurate 3D maps across diverse sensor configurations. For perception engineers and autonomy developers, this framework provides a practical way to produce metric-scale environmental maps in real time without sacrificing tracking stability
items.title: ScaRF-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Models and Classical Visual SLAM (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: ZeroWire Robotics has launched the Q8botOne, a smartphone-sized open-source quadruped robot featuring an innovative wire-free chassis where the main printed circuit board serves as the structural frame. Driven by an ESP32-C3 microcontroller and eight DYNAMIXEL smart bus actuators with parallel-linkage legs, the compact robot can walk, trot, jump, and carry twice its 250-gram payload.
items.title: Q8botOne: A Palm-Sized Open-Source Quadruped Robot with Smart Actuators (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in one affected user's device, bought from Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, pointing to tampering after manufacturing rather than a breach of Ledger itself. Mark Karpelès published images of a modified Nano X with a small board behind the screen and cellular components, which would presumably capture the 24-word recovery phrase as it displays during setup, leaving the secure element untouched.
items.title: Ledger confirms a hardware implant in a tampered wallet as suspected losses near $93M (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ting-Wei Sun pleaded guilty to four counts, including conspiracy to violate export controls, in a scheme that routed about $2.5 billion of Nvidia-powered servers through a Southeast Asian company to buyers in China.
items.title: Super Micro “fixer” pleads guilty in $2.5B scheme to divert Nvidia servers to China (3 minute read)

items.title: Jumper: An Open-Source Crab Robot with Walking and Jumping Capabilities (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: EasyNav 0.5.0 has officially launched, delivering an accessible yet comprehensive open-source navigation stack with upgraded path planning, improved recovery behaviors, and reduced compute overhead for ROS 2 systems.
items.title: EasyNav 0.5.0 Navigation System Released for ROS 2 Distributions (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple's new HomeView device is a seven-inch tablet that starts at $299. It can recognize up to six members of a household and change its content based on who is using it. There is a countertop version and a version that can be mounted on a wall. The HomeView will be available for purchase starting on November 13.
items.title: Apple Introduces HomeView, a $299 Tablet for the Home (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google's flagship Gemini 4 Argon multimodal language AI model is now broadly available. Developers and enterprises now have a powerful new option for software engineering, financial analysis, legal work, cybersecurity, and scientific research. API prices have been discounted substantially for a limited time. Argon is available through the paid Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Antigravity, eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions, and to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers through the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.
items.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Argon broadly available with limited-time low API pricing of 2/10 per 1M token (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX plans to perform as many as 456 launches and 912 landings at its Texas facility each year. The company's CEO, Elon Musk, has been open about the company's intent to launch Starship as rapidly as possible in the future. He has claimed that, in less than a decade, SpaceX will be able to launch Starship more than once every hour. SpaceX recently announced plans to invest as much as $100 billion to build a massive launch site in southern Louisiana to support rapid Starship launches.
items.title: SpaceX Plan to Launch 456 Starships a Year in Texas Under Review (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Science Corporation's vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, is commercially available in Europe for patients who have lost their sight to an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, but the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases. It recently implanted the chip in a patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. The company's work with PRIMA is part of a broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface. It envisions a future where BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications rather than just being used to control computers.
items.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: There are four types of ambition. Speed gets the same work done in less time. Altitude involves going up in abstraction and considering the outcome rather than the individual task. Depth considers a task the way a field-leading expert would, going one level deeper and touching the underlying data, tools, and problems. Range draws on multiple fields rather than just the one the task might need at the surface using knowledge, tools, and techniques you normally wouldn't.
items.title: How to be more ambitious: A tutorial for humans with models (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic was being bottlenecked by developer infrastructure built for human scale, so it built an in-house version control system called Scion to support its next stage of growth, and fully migrated its monorepo from git in five months. It also built and shipped a code review surface, code search, a rich source control IAM system, novel ways of managing and landing large amounts of reviewed code, and more, all in that same time period. Anthropic averaged about 2,500 code changes merged per day in May. It now merges over 30,000 per day, and the rate of growth isn't expected to slow down anytime soon.
items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic (23 minute read)

items.summary_html: Blue-collar workers typically do the hands-on labor of making or fixing stuff. Software developers have tried to separate themselves from this category, but they also make or fix stuff, just in bits rather than atoms. Just like electricians or carpenters, software developers must spend years practicing their craft in order to become skilled and sought-after. Just like anyone else in a skilled trade, software engineers can be outpaced by technology.
items.title: Were we blue-collar workers all along? (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI discovered a hidden recording device in one of its offices recently. It was traced to Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi Arabian national who joined the company's product team in July 2025 as an engineer. He was arrested by the FBI. The device was built to evade detection and used advanced encryption. It could monitor audio and had a way to transfer data without being noticed.
items.title: FBI Arrests OpenAI Employee Accused of Planting Bug in Office (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cloudflare's data pipeline handles roughly two billion events per second while hardware capacity grows more slowly than traffic. Product-specific schemas, zstd compression, later replication, earlier sampling, and aggregation have collectively deferred the equivalent of two and a half years of hardware expansion.
items.title: Rewinding the Exponential: How We Keep Hardware Usage Down (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic replaced Git with Scion after daily merges grew from roughly 2,500 to more than 30,000. The centralized system uses server-side commits, sparse checkouts, and layered caches, reducing its source control infrastructure's CPU and memory footprint by 200 times and freeing 25% of CI CPU capacity.
items.title: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Relace explains how it built a small model that applies code edits at a reported 10,000 tokens per second using high-quality merge data, LoRA fine-tuning, FP8 quantization, and speculative decoding. Its training pipeline filtered 200,000 candidate examples down to about 145,000, using a judge calibrated against 500 manually reviewed merges. Relace Apply 3 supports a 256,000-token context and multiple diff formats, although improving frontier-model edit accuracy could eventually reduce the need for specialized apply models.
items.title: A Year of Fast Apply: The Path to 10k Tokens per Second (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Programming for curiosity and enjoyment can restore motivation without requiring a business case or a finished product. This presentation suggests small experiments, toy implementations, language exploration, and documenting the process, with permission to switch projects or stop when they stop being fun.
items.title: Recreational Programming (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: More ambitious AI use can mean pursuing higher-level outcomes, applying expert methods to raw data, or combining ideas from multiple fields. Practical examples show how to move beyond generating a quarterly slide deck toward identifying urgent decisions, testing assumptions, and validating results with independent tools.
items.title: How to Be More Ambitious: A Tutorial for Humans with Models (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: TanStack Start 1.0 is now stable and ready for production, formalizing a commitment to its APIs after extensive real-world use. It combines type-safe routing with server rendering, typed server functions, and middleware spanning client and server, while shipping current agent guidance through TanStack Intent.
items.title: TanStack Start 1.0 Is Stable (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini 4 Argon for complex software engineering, scientific research, robotics, and professional workflows. The model offers a one-million-token output window, and Google reports uses ranging from large Chromium refactors to physics-ready robot simulations and vulnerability remediation.
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon (Website)

items.summary_html: Physical Intelligence's API beta lets developers upload robot demonstrations, fine-tune its models on managed infrastructure, and run inference through a hosted gateway. Early partners independently improved policies across manufacturing and other applications, although some deployments exposed network connectivity challenges.
items.title: Frontier Models for Every Robot: Announcing the Pi API Beta (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Two-thirds of the Forbes AI 50 companies use some form of usage-based pricing as variable AI costs push businesses toward hybrid subscriptions, credits, and outcome charges. Examples from AI companies show why spending controls, flexible packaging, measurable customer value, and pricing pages readable by both people and agents are becoming part of the product.
items.title: The “Alien” Economics of AI Monetization (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Federal prosecutors charged an OpenAI engineer with using or attempting to use a device to intercept conversations after a concealed recorder was found in an executive conference room. OpenAI says it referred the discovery to the FBI and has found no indication that model weights, source code, or customer data were improperly accessed or taken.
items.title: OpenAI Engineer Arrested over Alleged Conference Room Bugging (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: In ten runs on one Java API service, a behavioral harness raised GPT-6 Luna's acceptance rate from three successes to ten, while GPT-6 Sol passed all ten runs with or without it. Harnessed Luna cost about 33% less per run than unharnessed Sol, but those estimates exclude harness maintenance and the unusually detailed brief limits how broadly the results apply.
items.title: Are Harnesses Worth the Cost? (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI deployment companies embed engineers inside enterprises to connect models to real workflows, build evaluations, and manage the organizational changes needed to turn model capabilities into business results.
items.title: The Rise of DeployCos (7 minute read)

items.title: Pulse Local (Website)

items.title: I Posted to HN, and Then My Website Was Flooded with AI Bot Traffic (3 minute read)

items.title: Bifrost (GitHub Repo)

Prosecutors alleged the device was used to covertly intercept conversations, while OpenAI said it found no evidence that model weights, source code, or customer data were accessed.
items.title: OpenAI Employee Arrested Over Hidden Recording Device (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google made Gemini 4 Argon available on Google Cloud as a frontier model for long, multi-step enterprise work. It was positioned for tasks requiring sustained context and domain expertise, including software development, finance, legal work, and cybersecurity.
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon Lands on Google Cloud (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The debate over AI consciousness continues with minimal progress, as many argue without strong evidence. Anthropic's new policy classifies abusive behavior towards AI, such as Claude, as a violation of terms to cultivate positive model interactions. Despite skepticism from many, some, including Nick Bostrom, believe current AIs may be conscious, complicating ethical considerations around AI development.
items.title: Arguments About AI Consciousness Remain Highly Motivated and At Best Overconfident (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Splitting a task among several AI agents creates another job: deciding who does what, passing information between them, and checking their results. Anthropic's dynamic workflows let Claude write the program that manages those steps. An October 12 demonstration assigned stock tickers to separate agents, then reviewed their findings before producing a report. The presenters said this found more detail but cost much more than using one agent. Developers can set a session spending limit, but the running model does not know that budget.
items.title: How Anthropic's Dynamic Workflows Coordinate Claude Agents (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24B-parameter reasoning model with 2B active parameters, is designed for fast, private on-device agents. It outperforms or matches larger models like Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on five out of eight benchmarks and runs up to 1.7x faster due to its efficient architecture. Available on Hugging Face, it supports extensive inference frameworks, making it suitable for tasks needing swift local inference and tool usage.
items.title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nvidia is making the full NVIDIA Run:ai platform available as open-source software. It is now possible for every NVIDIA DSX ecosystem partner and AI cloud to increase workload throughput, improve GPU utilization, and operate shared AI infrastructure more efficiently and effectively. The release includes the complete NVIDIA Run:ai platform, KAI Scheduler, GPU Fractioning Operator, KAI Resource Management, and Workload Map. Platform teams and ecosystem partners can adopt NVIDIA Run:ai as an integrated whole, build on it for their own products and services, or integrate individual components based on their requirements.
items.title: NVIDIA Run:ai Is Now Open Source as Part of NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Physical Intelligence is making its latest models available for training and inference through the Pi API beta. The Pi API adapts the latest and most powerful robotic foundation models to each application, dealing with ML infrastructure, compute, and complex data pipelines. Users just upload data, launch fine-tuning on managed compute and infrastructure, and access the fine-tuned models via a hosted gateway to run inference.
items.title: Frontier Models for Every Robot (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenCode 2.0 contains quite a lot of new features, performance improvements, and bug fixes. The server now automatically runs as a single background process. Programmatic clients will autodiscover the local service and just work. OpenCode can now be used as a library with the SDK package. More details about the update are available in the article.
items.title: OpenCode 2.0 (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ramp has launched Glass, an AI workspace that shares company knowledge, reusable skills, and collaborative sessions across teams. Employees have made 6,500+ knowledge edits, while model routing cut AI costs by 30% and automated workflows dramatically expanded feature-request tracking.
items.title: Ramp Glass (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Character.ai initiated a voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy process to pursue a court-supervised sale after facing legal, regulatory, and operational pressures. The company said the platform could continue under a successful bid, but may be wound down if no viable buyer emerges.
items.title: Character.ai Filed for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy (2 minute read)

items.title: SpaceXSI bundles X Premium, Grok, and Cursor into one subscription (2 minute read)

items.title: Introducing CLiF: Continual Learning from Full-Stack Trajectories (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: AMD's Helion agentic AI rack is designed for flexible AI infrastructure that caters to hyperscale deployments and enterprise needs. It supports a range of configurations, including CPU-only and GPU-integrated systems, aligning with diverse AI workloads. Helion, part of an upcoming open blueprint by AMD for OCP, is set for release in November.
items.title: Introducing AMD Helion, Agentic AI Compute at Rack Scale (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Starting in 2027, Microsoft will deploy Maia at multi-gigawatt scale and make it the main inference system for its products. The next-generation Maia 300 uses compute chiplets on TSMC's N2P process and targets long-context, multi-step agent workloads. Digitimes reports that the supply chain is already preparing for a surge in server builds in 2027.
items.title: Microsoft takes Maia to multi-gigawatt scale, making it the default inference chip for its own products (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: This deep dive uses the Emmy compiler framework to follow PyTorch operations down to CUDA one lowering stage at a time: Tensor IR, Loop IR, Tile IR, Kernel IR, and finally emitted code. It uses RMSNorm and matrix multiplication as worked examples. It also covers operator fusion, schedule selection, and online attention rewrites, so readers can see what Triton-style stacks do under the hood.
items.title: Building a GPU compiler from scratch, from PyTorch to CUDA (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Physical Intelligence opened a beta API for its π robotics foundation models: upload demonstrations, fine-tune on Pi-managed compute, and run the result on your own robot through a hosted inference gateway. Early partners spanned hardware from Actor's autonomous wheel loader, running a commercial deployment with no operator onboard, to Almond's dual-arm Axol, which learned to deburr its own spacers in four days. Since most ran cloud-hosted inference, network connectivity was a pain point for some.
items.title: Physical Intelligence opens a beta API to fine-tune and host π robot models (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple Silicon Macs have powerful GPUs that sit mostly idle in normal use. Minions combines them across machines into a virtual GPU cloud for large ML inference jobs, with fault tolerance and flexible task scheduling. The pitch is that teams can use hardware they already own instead of waiting for expensive, centralized GPU capacity.
items.title: Apple's Minions pools idle Macs into a virtual GPU cloud (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team ran Gemma4-26B-A4B across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes with 4GB of RAM each, using pipeline parallelism at 0.39 tokens per second, to test whether small models could replicate across cheap IoT hardware. A 9B model got inference running on 8 of 9 hardware types tested, and a Kimwolf-sized botnet would total only about 40 H100s of compute. By their trend line, small models reach the needed capability in simplified tests by year-end.
items.title: Anthropic runs a 26B model across 15 $55 TV boxes to test IoT self-replication (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: An Abilene-scale build requires roughly $17B for chips and servers, $3B for power, and only $2.4B for construction. Transformers, generators, and cooling equipment face long lead times and rising prices.
items.title: What a 1GW AI data center costs: about $30B, and $17B of it is chips (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple's Home Collection, built with LG and Schneider Electric, covers cameras, thermostats, sensors, a doorbell, and a deadbolt. LG's lock uses Ultra Wideband to unlock as you approach and works locally over Matter and Aliro, while its indoor cam physically tilts away when someone's home. Every device supports Thread, and cameras keep recording to built-in storage if Wi-Fi drops. Prices run $199.95 to $399.95, with availability starting in December.
items.title: Apple Home Collection brings LG and Schneider cameras, a lock, and thermostats to Apple Home (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Crescent Island, Intel's data center inference GPU, will be sold as the GPU D-Series.
items.title: Intel names Crescent Island the GPU D-Series, with 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8 and up to 480GB of LPDDR5X (3 minute read)

items.title: How Meta builds AI networks: IcePack, Tahan and open-source MetaRoCE (7 minute read)

items.title: SK Hynix's H-TPU spreads SSD controller work across more than 100 tiny in-house cores (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: GTA VI is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment releases in history when it comes out on November 19. Its immediate predecessor is the best-selling nonmobile game of all time. The game's release is causing other entertainment companies to delay products until next year because they know GTA VI will suck up the planet's attention for most of November. It will almost certainly be the most expensive video game ever created. This article looks at how Rockstar Games built what is expected to be the biggest video game blockbuster of all time.
items.title: The Making of Grand Theft Auto VI (28 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic told investors recently that the company's revenue for the third quarter jumped about 45% from the prior quarter to $16.8 billion. The AI lab is currently pursuing what may become the largest-ever initial public offering. Its IPO could value the company at $2 trillion. The San Francisco company is expected to begin trading as early as next month. A successful launch from Anthropic could reopen the door for other listings and provide a vote of confidence for the industry.

items.summary_html: NASA's Perseverance rover has now driven 28.1 miles on Mars' surface, surpassing the distance that Opportunity covered from 2004 to 2018. Perseverance landed on Mars in February 2021 and has been traveling in and around the Jezero Crater since. It was set to surpass the driving record back in August, but it came across some interesting rocks, so it dawdled for two months. Perseverance most likely still has many miles to go in the coming years. This article contains some of the highlights from its drive so far.
items.title: 28 Miles and Counting: NASA's Perseverance Rover Sets a Mars Driving Record (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Two NASA missions are on track to launch to Venus in the early 2030s. The Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging (DAVINCI), which will send a parachute-assisted descent probe through Venus' atmosphere, is now scheduled for launch in December 2030. The Venus Emissivity, Radio science, InSAR, Topography, And Spectroscopy (VERITAS) mission will launch in November 2032 to map the Venusian surface by radar from orbit. The European Space Agency is building an orbiter for launch to Venus in 2032, and Rocket Lab plans to launch a privately funded probe as soon as next year to search for signs of organic material in the planet's clouds.
items.title: Things are finally looking up for NASA's first missions to Venus in a generation (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Being able to tell clean code from messy code is still useful, but it's becoming something that tools can help with. Knowing what shape a program should have before anyone writes it is something AI still can't do yet. The best way to get better at AI coding might be to spend more time thinking about problems and less time thinking about prompts. The programmers that get the most out of these tools already knew what they wanted.

items.summary_html: Giving AI agents a way to independently verify their work heavily improves the quality of output. Write end-to-end tests that simulate real user flows and act as the ground truth. Use property-based testing to specify what should never happen and generate thousands of test cases that attempt to break those constraints. Require tests to run quickly and deterministically so that agents retry when the loop is slow or unreliable.
items.title: Agentic Verification (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Reinforcement learning, on-policy distillation, and supervised fine-tuning on near-policy data change only a small fraction of parameters. Small and sparse are different claims. The expected gradient is a covariance, the Fisher is a variance, and the Fisher caps the gradient for any reward. At one position, the Fisher is the variance of logit sensitivities: whatever moves every candidate together counts for nothing. None of this needs on-policy sampling - it needs a score centered under the sampling distribution.
items.title: The Gradient Is a Covariance (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Doing reinforcement learning for agent use-cases is conceptually not at all that complicated. For each problem, you set up a VM with a harness and a fresh model context, send the prompt, let the model make tool calls, score the whole thing at the end, and update the weights. Agentic post-training means there's more than the model to consider. Even when the harness is consistent, you can still go off-policy with the trajectories themselves. Agents spawn subagents, make parallel tool calls, and compact large sessions, which adds complexity.

Some customers want to place orders for 2029 and 2030. Q4 sales are guided to €14.2 to €15.2 billion.
items.title: ASML says 2027 and 2028 tool supply won't meet demand as Q3 shipments hit 113 systems (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google ran magic state cultivation on its Willow chip, cutting errors about 40x versus uncultivated states and reaching a record 99.99% logical fidelity for T-states. Magic states are a bottleneck because making them could consume up to 95% of a quantum computer's capacity. Cultivation injects a noisy state into a small chip region, then uses coordinated measurements to discard flawed attempts, and Google grafted a distance-3 color code onto a distance-5 surface code. Larger-scale demonstrations are still needed.
items.title: Google's Willow chip cuts quantum magic-state errors 40x with cultivation (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: ServeTheHome toured AWS' in-house networking lab, covering switches from 3.2 Tbps to 102.4 Tbps (1.6T OSFP ports, not yet in volume), a 12.8 Tbps switch with 16 FPGAs encrypting every port, and a dedicated satellite-referenced timing network. It also saw 64-wavelength DWDM modules and hollow-core fiber with about 33% lower latency.
items.title: Inside the Secretive AWS Networking Lab (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Rocket Lab moved Neutron's debut to 2027 after finding voids in the carbon-composite layers of the forward dome on its first-stage propellant tank. A replacement dome is being built, and Rocket Lab must still inspect it, assemble the first stage, and complete pressure and cryogenic tests before setting a firm date. It's the rocket's fourth slip since its 2021 unveiling, following a January tank rupture in testing, and shares fell about 10% after hours.
items.title: Rocket Lab delays Neutron to 2027 over voids in a carbon-composite tank dome (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ayar Labs and GUC simulated a 105mm by 140mm package with two XPUs, eight HBM4 stacks, and eight TeraPHY optical engines, offering over 100 Tbps of optical bandwidth at more than 3 kW. A standard air heatsink at 5 to 6 m/s failed spec, while an impingement liquid cold plate at 4.5 L/min kept the optical engines under 100°C. Results use static power assumptions, so dynamic workload simulation is next.
items.title: Ayar Labs and GUC simulate a 3 kW co-packaged optics package, and only liquid cooling holds spec (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Monazite ore is 45 to 70 percent rare earths by weight and carries all four elements motor magnets need (neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium), making it a leading path around China's roughly 90 percent market share. The catch is thorium, whose waste must be stored indefinitely. Energy Fuels already produces neodymium-praseodymium oxide plus pilot dysprosium and terbium at its Utah mill, while Saskatchewan's government-backed plant has produced little after six years and over CA$100 million.
items.title: Monazite ore could supply EV motor magnet metals, if the thorium waste can be handled (19 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Delaware jury found Arm breached its architectural license with Qualcomm by failing to provide software patches and tools for its designs, and intentionally interfered with Qualcomm's Meta chip talks, but awarded just $2 in damages. Arm won five other breach claims, and Qualcomm's license runs through 2033, so its Oryon CPU work continues. Both sides claimed vindication, with Qualcomm shares up about 2.5% and Arm down about 2.2%.
items.title: Jury finds Arm breached Qualcomm's chip license but awards just $2 (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ukrainian officials say SpaceX capped speeds on military Starshield terminals mounted on drones, with no warning and no stated reason. The cap is nominally 160 km/h, but the 7th Rapid Reaction Corps reports 10- to 20-second connection drops at just 110 to 120 km/h, and a volunteer says drops now start at 60 to 70 km/h. Multiple missions were cancelled. Officials suspect it's intentional, and Ukrainian firm Stetman is developing an alternative satellite system, UASAT-NANO.
items.title: SpaceX reportedly speed-limits Starshield terminals on Ukrainian drones, cancelling missions (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA's RTX Spark pairs a Blackwell GPU with a Grace CPU and up to 128 GB of shared LPDDR5X, with laptops due October 16 and compact desktops in November.
items.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark: AI Platform, Laptop Chip and DLSS 5 (25 minute read)

items.summary_html: Amazon's Bee launched Bee Frontier, a wrist or clip-on AI recorder with dual noise-filtering microphones, IP67 water resistance, and seven days of battery, for $74.99.
items.title: Amazon's Bee launches a $75 wrist-worn AI recorder and a magnetic phone attachment with 21-day battery (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Reuters reports Solidigm wants US approval to ship more American chipmaking tools to SK Hynix's Dalian, China fab, as a condition of building a US NAND factory.
items.title: Solidigm reportedly ties a US NAND fab to more tool exports for SK Hynix's China plant (2 minute read)

items.title: Red Hat engineer uses Claude Code to reverse-engineer a scanner and fix a MIPI webcam on Linux (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple is already working on developing a higher-end version of its HomeView display with a robotic limb that can automatically swivel the screen toward whoever is speaking. The company's own advertising for the $299 HomeView makes a compelling case for why a motorized version is needed. The device was designed to be controlled primarily by voice. While the HomeView is a pretty nice offering for $299, its design clearly shows it was a product conceived years ago.
items.title: Apple's HomeView Offers Tantalizing Preview of a Future Robotic Version (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Virtually every major mutual fund company, insurer, and private equity firm, as well as scores of individual investors, has been buying up AI debt. Hyperscalers, which continue to borrow heavily, have been forced by investors to pay modestly more in interest in recent debt deals. The market is realising there may be a mismatch between the money committed and borrowed today and the ability to generate revenues down the road. An increasing number of data centers are being delayed by permitting issues, and in some instances falling through.
items.title: Weak Links Start to Show in AI Borrowing (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: It would be a terrible waste of resources to spend millions of dollars to formalize mathematics results in libraries nobody uses. Doing so could also disincentivize good research and productive use of AI, disrupt the social norms and practices research depends on, and set the field back decades. Several projects are now working to ensure formal libraries fulfill the community's mathematical goals. Within the next few years, most of mathematics will be able to be formalized in such a way that mathematicians can explore, build on, and make use of formal libraries. This will significantly extend their ability to develop and discover new mathematics.
items.title: How to Formalize All of Mathematics (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Researchers have discovered a signal deep in the brain that richly represents a stimulus people are unaware of. This finding makes it possible to understand how a pattern of neural activity accesses consciousness. There are clear signals that correspond to both what is and isn't conscious. This makes it possible to follow both sets of footprints and track down the full machine for generating conscious percepts.
items.title: We discovered something totally unexpected about the neural structure of consciousness (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Good products carry something of the people who make them. The industry often talks about software as if it comes out of a factory, but two teams can talk to similar customers and have access to the same technology and still make very different things. The difference is how each team understands what they see and the style they go about building it. The founder background or company DNA shapes this a lot.
items.title: Someone behind the software (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Decoherence is the accumulation of locally valid but mutually incompatible or redundant models within a system. It causes the cost of change to be dominated by translating among those models and preventing unintended side-effects. Decoherence grows relative to the rate of change of a system, and it increases faster the more decoherent a system is, resulting in runaway exponential growth. It rules out the specter of runaway recursive self-improvement, as decoherence both prevents AI from improving in a bubble and limits the rate at which it can improve outside of it. However, it also introduces a new kind of disaster called Decoherence Collapse.
items.title: Decoherence (48 minute read)

items.summary_html: Large language models have demonstrated remarkable abilities in generating mathematical proofs. This could lead to a golden age where a new generation of scientists is empowered, new STEM expertise is developed, and an open, collaborative, and intellectually independent scientific enterprise is preserved. However, it could also lead to independent human scientific activity progressively weakening, the production of new knowledge becoming increasingly concentrated in a small number of hands, and knowledge becoming alien to human understanding. The future will likely be a combination of these scenarios.
items.title: Will it be a golden age or a dark age for mathematics (and science)? (23 minute read)

items.summary_html: Terence Tao, one of the world's greatest living mathematicians, is currently doing very little math. OpenAI's recent finding in the mathematical field has left him feeling used, as he previously had a good relationship with many employees at the company. Now, he sees them as only using math to evaluate their models, and can't see a way to constructively engage. Despite OpenAI's releases, most problems at the frontiers of math are unsolved, and as math remains infinite, the difficulty of problems is boundless.
items.title: Why One of the World's Greatest Mathematicians Is on a ‘War Footing' (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: Gittifacts routes agent-written changes to auto-merge, quick review, or full review based on test evidence and repository policy, after a human approves the plan. Missing signals can only increase scrutiny, and feature flags make merged changes reversible. Auto-merge still relies on the submitting agent's test environment for some evidence, while evidence generation took 13 to 17 minutes per change on the project's own repository.
items.title: Humans approve intent, machines prove conformance (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: HybridAgent is a research approach for training AI agents to reason internally using numerical representations instead of writing out every intermediate thought, while still producing text to call tools such as Python or web search and deliver answers. In tests, a 14B Qwen3 model trained this way scored 52.4 on GAIA versus 43.7 for a matched text-only agent, with estimated decoding costs falling from $470 to $176 per million questions.
items.title: HybridAgent Thinks in Latent Space and Acts in Text (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: AWS Lambda Web Functions run standard Node.js HTTP servers without adapters, with each execution environment handling concurrent requests and streaming responses. In a sample run of 300 streaming requests with up to 200 open at once, five environments consumed 4.75 seconds of CPU. Billing covers active CPU, memory, and requests, so waiting on a database or API uses little CPU but still incurs other charges.
items.title: Exploring AWS Lambda Web Functions for building web applications (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Good products reflect a shared point of view shaped by experience, customer conversations, and judgment. When teams use agents to add features independently, individually useful changes can weaken the product's coherence unless someone keeps shaping the whole.
items.title: Someone Behind the Software (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Elegant systems often gain simplicity and scale by accepting limits on freshness, coordination, or flexibility. Coding agents tend to invent extra requirements, so explicitly stating which compromises are acceptable can prevent unnecessary locks, checks, and layers of abstraction.
items.title: What Requirements Don't You Have? (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Frameworks remain useful when agents write the code because they supply structure, shared maintenance, and familiar abstractions. Rewriting an application in a faster language can change behavior that users rely on, making targeted optimization and dependency updates a more practical starting point. Familiar code also makes it easier to review the decisions an agent makes.
items.title: Does Ruby on Rails Still Make Sense? (8 minute read)

items.title: DeepSeek Search & Fetch (Website)

items.summary_html: Sphinx pauses pushes to protected branches and quizzes developers on what agent-written code does, including failure scenarios. A separate reviewer reads the diff without seeing the development chat, explains incorrect answers, and asks a new scenario before allowing the push. It supports existing coding agents and configurable model endpoints, with a logged bypass for skipped checks.
items.title: Sphinx (Website)

items.summary_html: Rakazo is an open-source, self-hosted AI assistant for running persistent bots with their own memory, routines, and conversations. Bots can use browsers, terminals, files, and desktop interfaces, with your choice of model and local or hosted computer environments. The project is in beta and offers web, desktop, and mobile clients.
items.title: Rakazo (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: An internal Claude research model traced the seeds of five NIST prime curves to the lrand48 random-number generator initialized with Unix timestamps, explaining a decades-old provenance mystery. Anthropic says the findings strengthen confidence in the curves and do not reveal a cryptographic break. Some base-point origins, skipped candidates, and one binary-curve seed remain unexplained.
items.title: Claude Reveals ECDSA Curve Origins (9 minute read)

items.title: Search & Fetch (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 delivers substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. It also reduces task execution time and output length, advancing the performance-cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer KV cache reuse in Compressed Sparse Attention 2 with FP4 KV caching, reducing its global KV cache footprint to 890 bytes per token. Its persistent KV cache footprint is roughly 1/8 of that of DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The model delivers substantially better performance than the baseline despite its much smaller KV cache footprint.
items.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (Hugging Face Repo)

It credits AI-driven DRAM shortages, expanded capacity, and more output per wafer.
