items.title: CXMT swings to a nearly $20B nine-month profit as AI demand drives up DRAM prices (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: After moving Roman's secondary mirror by about one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, engineers measured 63 nanometers RMS of optical error in the Wide Field Instrument, nearly 30% better than the 90-nanometer requirement. The camera has 18 detectors, and the same adjustment fixed slight defocus in the Coronagraph Instrument, which still needs testing of its ability to block unwanted light. Roman launched August 30, and both instruments now match or beat predictions.
items.title: NASA's Roman telescope beats its image-quality spec by nearly 30% after a hair-width mirror nudge (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Roadster's floor uses fans and perimeter seals to pull air out from under the car, creating up to 2 g of suction, enough to hold it upside down while stationary, and at speed, front and rear passages open for more flow. Cold-gas thrusters add a second system: ten nozzles fed by compressed air, with all-electric actuators for fast micro-adjustments, which Tesla says push with four to five times the force tires can deliver.
items.title: Tesla Roadster pairs underbody suction fans with cold-gas thrusters for grip beyond what tires allow (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Variable frequency drives adjust motor speed to match demand, cutting a motor's energy use by about 40 to 60 percent. Toyota saved over $700,000 a year after putting them on 200-plus HVAC motors at its Kentucky plant, in a $1.25 million pilot. Cheaper sensors, machine-learning control, and power chips borrowed from EVs and solar inverters have cut costs. ABB claims drives on every motor could cover up to five years of data center load growth.
items.title: Variable frequency drives could free up grid power by cutting motor energy use 40 to 60 percent (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Argonne and UIUC researchers coupled spin waves in a thin yttrium iron garnet film to a superconducting resonator built directly on top, creating a hybrid mode that propagates one way and could keep return noise from leaking back into qubits. The key materials fix was swapping the usual rare-earth-containing substrate, which absorbs microwaves at low temperatures, for one without rare-earth metals. It's still a proof of concept.
items.title: Spin waves coupled to a superconducting circuit create a one-way street for microwave signals (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Kornia-SLAM is an open-source visual-inertial odometry and spatial mapping library implemented entirely in Rust. It supports monocular, stereo, and RGB-D cameras coupled with inertial measurement units, utilizing factor graph optimization to maintain real-time performance and strict memory safety. This framework gives embedded software teams a reliable, crash-resilient foundation for real-time spatial estimation on compute-limited physical devices.
items.title: Kornia-SLAM: Visual-Inertial Odometry and SLAM in Rust (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 4 Argon, a multimodal foundation model engineered specifically for embodied physical systems. Featuring native spatio-temporal reasoning and low-latency action generation, it links high-level semantic understanding directly to robot execution through native bridges for ROS 2 and physics simulators like MuJoCo. The architecture allows creators of intelligent physical machines to translate natural language goals into dexterous, real-world manipulation and navigation.
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Multimodal Foundation Models for Embodied Intelligence (4 minute read)

items.title: AMD shows how to hand-tune an FP16 GEMM kernel on RDNA 3 and RDNA 4 to match hipBLASLt (25 minute read)

items.title: Terminal RViz: Terminal-Based 3D Visualizer for ROS 2 (2 minute read)

items.title: ASPIRE: Agentic Skill Discovery and Policy Synthesis (3 minute read)

items.title: Apple and Meta tune an 816B-parameter open model to run on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios (3 minute read)

items.title: HUMXN pays for home repairs in three cities to record wearable-sensor data for robot training (3 minute read)

The company has already ordered thousands of cars from China to help expand its fleet. Waymo currently operates 4,000 vehicles in 15 cities in the US.
items.title: Waymo plans to quintuple its fleet (1 minute read)

The company will also introduce a new low-end MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, a refreshed iMac, and a revamped iPad mini with a sharper screen. Apple retail stores are preparing to begin selling new products on November 6. The new touch MacBooks, which will run on M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, will have a Dynamic Island interface, as well as a sharper OLED display.
items.title: Apple Announces Oct. 28 Event for Touch-Screen MacBook Pro (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis is a weaker version of the Riemann hypothesis, arguably the biggest open question in math. Resolving the Riemann hypothesis would enable mathematicians to better understand the nature of prime numbers. OpenAI's recently released proof for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis is the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far, by quite a margin. The vast majority of the consequences of resolving it already follow from solving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now? (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Endurance Energy, a Seattle-based startup, recently demonstrated the technical feasibility of using an active underwater volcano to generate electricity. The startup deployed a 3-ton prototype power plant at the Axial Seamount in the northeast Pacific Ocean in September and generated less than 10 seconds of net-positive electricity. The company's next trial run, planned for the winter of 2026 to 2027, will aim to sustain higher power generation. It is currently developing a 2-megawatt commercial generator for its first planned commercial deployment with the Kingdom of Tonga in 2027.
items.title: Startup taps underwater volcano as energy source in “proof point” test (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Clairic is an extraction model. Extraction models are a new class of System One-style models that can extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs, all at significantly higher accuracy, faster latency, and lower cost than traditional LLMs. It answers with values directly extracted from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it. The model can't produce a mistyped answer or hallucinate in the same way an LLM can, but it can still make mistakes.
items.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cloudflare lowered its average review cost from $2.43 to $0.77. The biggest single saving came from checking what actually reached the provider on each session's first request, and finding a way to order those messages in a way that was as consistent as possible across commits, merge requests, and repositories. Check whether each session's first request actually reads from the cache and whether reviewers still find real problems at the effort level being paid for.
items.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Some worry about radiology being totally automated, but the more likely outcome is a future where there is more demand for services as predictive power increases. This is similar to how programming is thriving despite drastic change in the field. It may be possible one day to use radiology images to predict disease probabilities far into the future. It will manage AI workloads such as vision inference and LiDAR data processing in the Moon's high-radiation, atmosphere-free environment. NASA and Deloitte are joining this mission to enhance AI capabilities, including Federated Learning and predictive cyber-analytics.
items.title: HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 Will Bring AI and HPC to the Moon on Astrolab FLIP (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX launched its Starfall return capsule for the second time on the Bandwagon-5 rideshare, one of 32 payloads on a Falcon 9 booster flying for the 19th time. Per an FAA assessment, the disk-shaped capsule is about 10 feet wide and weighs 4,600 pounds, and can bring 2,200 pounds of payload home, aimed at microgravity research and in-space manufacturing. It deployed last, 2 hours 48 minutes after liftoff, alongside Varda's W-Series 7 capsule.
items.title: SpaceX flies its Starfall return capsule for the second time on a 32-payload rideshare (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: This article presents views from Synopsys, Keysight, Renesas, Arteris, Cadence, and Mixel on how physical AI changes chip design. Engineers must handle unpredictable environments, safety and serviceability, and split designs between devices that can rely on the cloud and those that must run fully locally, such as vehicles. Several speakers frame it as a sensing and imaging problem as much as a compute one.
items.title: Why Physical AI Is So Hard To Engineer (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI will soon be superhuman at hardware design, but the digital-to-physical interface is lossy. Building real parts means navigating CNC/CAM translation, tolerance stacking, vendors, and scale, while measuring reality is sparse, slow, expensive, and sometimes qualitative. Demand is expected to shift toward suppliers of machined parts, harnesses, and components, plus better simulation and process-knowledge data.
items.title: AI hardware design is the easy part, the lossy physical interface is the bottleneck (15 minute read)

items.title: Infineon Targets Semiconductor Market for Humanoid Robotic Hands (3 minute read)

items.title: Monarch Quantum supplies photonics for NASA's planned space-based quantum gravity gradiometer (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's Claude Duet joins a fast-growing field of AI assistants that take actions and perform tasks on their own. Unlike OpenAI's dots and Meta's Muse, Anthropic's agent was built for work and is less capable at personal errands. It can connect to more than 6,000 outside apps and make purchases through Link, Stripe's digital wallet, and Shopify's Shop Pay. The agent shows users exactly what it plans to do before performing actions, and some actions, like trading stocks or moving money between accounts, are blocked even with user approval. The wait list to use the agent is now open to Anthropic's Pro and Max plan subscribers.
items.title: Anthropic Joins the AI Agent Race With Claude Duet (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Elon Musk is fully behind a combination of SpaceX and Tesla, his two most valuable companies. He is pushing to announce a deal by the first half of 2027 so it closes during the Trump administration. The timing will depend on when Tesla's board gets comfortable with the details - SpaceX shareholder approval is less of an obstacle, as Musk controls more than 80% of the voting power. Combining the companies before the end of this administration would consolidate Musk's corporate power before a potentially less accommodating political and financial environment takes hold.
items.title: Musk Tries to Lock In His Tesla-SpaceX Dream Before Trump's Exit (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tesla has started production of its Optimus humanoid robot at its factory in Fremont, California. While the company admits there is still more work to be done before the robot is fully safe and reliable, it says it has proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product. Elon Musk says Tesla will be able to make 20,000 units per week by the end of 2027. Tesla's profits fell 43% in the third quarter due to heavy investments in its Optimus robots, AI, and autonomous driving.
items.title: Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43% (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Physicists at Northwestern University have coaxed a single positron (the antimatter counterpart of an electron) into an exquisitely controlled quantum state for the first time. The scientists cooled the fast-moving particle to nearly absolute zero after capturing it from radioactive decay, and then suspended it in a near-perfect vacuum, resulting in a state where the positron behaved much like an artificial atom with quantum energy levels scientists can precisely control and observe. The technique could enable the most precise test yet of a fundamental symmetry between electrons and their antimatter counterparts.
items.title: Physicists trap and tame single particle of antimatter for months (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Git traffic grew exponentially over the past year. During that time, GitHub started moving almost all of its repositories to Azure. This post discusses how per-reference quorums will bring over the rest, and how object storage lets reads scale independently.
items.title: The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: An agent is three things: a model, an agentic loop, and a set of tools. Where these run has implications for cost, capability, effectiveness, and security. If you focus on topology, you can break down any agentic product and reason about what a product can and cannot do. There isn't one perfect loop - good UX for a general-purpose chatbot is not the same as good UX for a coding agent.
items.title: The Topology of an LLM Agent Loop With Tool Use (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI has discovered critical security vulnerabilities in PHP, prompting the US National Security Agency to advise organizations using PHP to either update immediately or take their systems offline until they can. Node.js has released an update that fixes four high-severity vulnerabilities. LiteLLM was compromised by an attacker who injected malicious code. eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, had its private keys compromised, potentially allowing attackers to issue fraudulent certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. These unrelated issues highlight the challenges cybersecurity teams now face.
items.title: The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: California's proposed tax on billionaires prompted Mark Zuckerberg to leverage the board at Meta to get the company to protect him from it. He issued an ultimatum to the board on September 9 that he would sell his home in Palo Alto, and the listing would be public, if a deal wasn't struck by September 13. The board decided to issue a new class of stock to shareholders that Zuckerberg could sell to pay the potential wealth tax without cutting into his 60.6% voting power. California's proposal would assess a one-time 5% tax on all holdings of billionaires who lived in California as of January 1, 2026.
items.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California's Proposed Wealth Tax (6 minute read)

Moving behavioral analytics out of Postgres also replaced disruptive retention cleanups with TTL rules and simplified data pipelines through materialized views.
items.title: Front-end Observability at Scale with ClickHouse (11 minute read)

items.title: The Web Is More Than Enough (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: An LLM's stated confidence is generated text, so a precise-looking number should not be treated as a calibrated measure of correctness. The proposed alternative derives scores from observable evidence and historical outcomes, then checks calibration regularly on the same kinds of tasks.
items.title: Asking LLM for Confidence (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Five imagined coffee purchases in 2035 illustrate different models of data control, from state surveillance and privacy regulation to commercial data markets, public infrastructure, and biometric identity. Privacy increasingly depends on who can stop collection. AI assistants and paid privacy tiers will make that question more pressing.
items.title: Who Holds the Off Switch? (24 minute read)

items.title: Claude Duet (Website)

items.summary_html: Omnara is an open-source managed agent platform that can run with different model providers and execute tools on sandboxes or your own machines. A REST API, TypeScript SDK, CLI, and dashboard expose agent runs, while a Postgres event log lets workers resume them after crashes.
items.title: Omnara (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Slower transistor scaling, memory bottlenecks, and power limits are renewing the case for specialized AI inference hardware. Matching different inference phases to different accelerators can improve performance per watt while adding deployment and software complexity and leaving room for GPUs to absorb successful ideas.
items.title: Why Hardware Specialization Is Back (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's Jalapeño inference chip links 64 dedicated cores to individual HBM memory banks to reduce data movement and improve utilization. This interview explains the tradeoff in memory-management complexity, the choice to keep prefill and decode on fungible hardware, and how AI-assisted optimization accelerated chip design and kernel development.
items.title: Inside OpenAI's Jalapeño AI Chip (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Reliable evaluation of open-ended agent tasks combines calibrated human judgments, automated judges or rubrics, and production monitoring. Power analysis, confidence intervals, and repeated runs help distinguish improvements from noise, while realistic, diverse tasks, and production feedback keep benchmarks useful.

items.summary_html: Recursive Flint is a mixture-of-experts model built for fast agentic coding on local hardware. It has 40 billion total parameters but activates just 2.5 billion per token. It was built from scratch by a small team of people and agents in under four months. Flint generates more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and more than 150 tokens per second on a 64GB NVIDIA RTX Spark at short contexts. It can be used as a daily coding model to complete tasks locally without sending data to a remote server.
items.title: Introducing Flint (7 minute read)

The integration will give customers native access to these models to power complex agentic workflows at scale. It will pair OpenAI's frontier models with Google Cloud's built-in access controls, centralized data governance, and high-performance infrastructure to support demanding enterprise workloads. OpenAI models will soon be available in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent.
items.title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud (2 minute read)

items.title: If Intelligence Is Getting Cheap, What Remains Expensive? (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude Mods flips the agent harness paradigm to face the human, creating a customizable "Attention Interface" for Claude AI. Mods are TypeScript or JavaScript functions that alter Claude Code's behavior in real-time, allowing users to design how Claude interacts with them. This shift lets users program the human-agent interface and even have Claude build mods, enhancing workflow and decision-making.
items.title: Claude Mods: Flipping the Harness Inside Out (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Language models can encode messages in images. These messages can be decoded by the same language model even if no information about the encoding method is passed. The act of decoding the hidden messages is obvious if the tool calls of the decoding model are monitored. The encoded messaging is surprisingly hard to spot, and it could be used as a precursor to steganography in images.
items.title: How does Fable 5.1 hide messages in images? (15 minute read)
